verdict.rationale: Conductor offers cloud workspaces and sandboxes, and its docs refer to install and setup scripts that an agent can edit while it configures the cloud computer. That implies a per-repository setup mechanism, but the evidence never documents how a developer declares dependencies, defines setup steps directly, or gets a reproducible environment across workspaces. Missing for 10: first-party docs on the environment/setup-script configuration format, explicit reproducibility guarantees (e.g. snapshots or images reused per workspace), how dependencies are declared, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can configure a reproducible cloud environment with the dependencies and setup steps my repository needs

citations.quote: You can also have an agent configure the computer for you: it can test your repositories, edit setup scripts, and run builds.
The agent can test your repositories, update install and setup scripts, and run builds — without asking you to confirm each step.
Sandboxes spin up in seconds, and agents keep working after you close your laptop.
